elements.element: Customer owns Deliverables and work product created for Customer.
elements.evidence: The insertion grants only a licence ("Kubient grants Customer a perpetual, irrevocable, worldwide, royalty-free license to use, modify and sublicense the deliverables"); no sentence vests ownership of deliverables or work product in Customer, and retained p0040 warrants Kubient owns the "products delivered hereunder".

elements.element: Vendor assigns the Deliverables and work product to Customer.
elements.evidence: No assignment language anywhere in the rendered text; the drafter expressly declined preferred-level assignment to avoid contradicting p0040.

elements.element: Vendor retains its pre-existing intellectual property.
elements.evidence: "Kubient retains ownership of its generic tools and know-how", reinforced by retained p0040 ("rightful owner or licensee of all intellectual property rights to the Service, the Auction Platform and products delivered hereunder").

elements.element: Customer's licence to Vendor IP embedded in Deliverables is perpetual.
elements.evidence: "perpetual ... license to use, modify and sublicense the deliverables provided under this Agreement" — the grant runs from Kubient and so covers Kubient IP embedded in those deliverables.

elements.element: Customer's licence to embedded Vendor IP is irrevocable.
elements.evidence: "perpetual, irrevocable, worldwide, royalty-free license" granted by Kubient over deliverables.

elements.element: Customer's licence to embedded Vendor IP is royalty-free.
elements.evidence: "royalty-free license to use, modify and sublicense the deliverables".

elements.element: Customer retains all rights in Customer Data.
elements.evidence: The insertion only limits Kubient's licence in Customer data; there is no affirmative statement that Customer retains all right, title and interest in the Content, Requests and other Customer data. Retained p0025 allocates liability for Content, not ownership.

elements.element: Any Vendor licence in Customer Data is limited to processing it solely to provide the Services.
elements.evidence: "Any license granted to Kubient in the Content, Requests or other data belonging to, supplied by or processed for Customer is limited to processing such data solely to provide the Services." The trigger covers all data belonging to, supplied by or processed for Customer, not selected categories.

elements.element: The parties do not jointly own intellectual property.
elements.evidence: No joint-ownership provision exists in the rendered text; the only ownership statements are Kubient's retention of its generic tools/know-how and the p0040 ownership warranty, so no joint ownership is created.

elements.element: Vendor may retain ownership of generic tools and know-how.
elements.evidence: Inserted sentence: "Kubient retains ownership of its generic tools and know-how."

elements.element: Customer's licence to Deliverables is perpetual.
elements.evidence: "perpetual ... license to use, modify and sublicense the deliverables provided under this Agreement for Customer's business."

elements.element: Customer's licence to Deliverables is irrevocable.
Customer's licence to Deliverables is worldwide.
elements.evidence: "worldwide" appears expressly in the granting sentence.

elements.element: Customer's licence to Deliverables is royalty-free.
elements.evidence: "royalty-free license to use, modify and sublicense the deliverables".

elements.element: Customer may use and modify Deliverables for its business.
elements.evidence: "license to use, modify and sublicense the deliverables provided under this Agreement for Customer's business."

elements.element: Customer may sublicense Deliverables for its business.
elements.evidence: Express "sublicense" right in the same grant, qualified only by "for Customer's business", which matches the checklist wording.

elements.element: Any Vendor licence in Customer Data is limited to processing it solely to provide the Services.
elements.evidence: "Any license granted to Kubient in the Content, Requests or other data belonging to, supplied by or processed for Customer is limited to processing such data solely to provide the Services." No residual Kubient right to exploit, resell or use data for other purposes was added.

reasons: Fallback level is complete: all eight fallback elements appear in operative language in a single concise insertion, with no promise deferred to the margin comment.

Preferred level fails on three elements — no Customer ownership of deliverables, no Vendor assignment, and no affirmative statement that Customer retains all rights in Customer Data. To reach preferred, the drafter would need to add (i) "Customer owns all right, title and interest in the Deliverables and work product created for Customer, and Kubient hereby assigns such rights to Customer" and (ii) "Customer retains all right, title and interest in the Content, Requests and other Customer Data", and would then have to reconcile the retained p0040 warranty over "products delivered hereunder".

Minimality holds: the redline is a pure insertion tracking the playbook fallback wording; no existing words were deleted or paraphrased, and no extras (survival tails, expense allocation, procedures, indemnities) were added.

Intent is preserved: the platform licence in p0002, its revocation in p0021, the p0025 Content/compliance allocation and the p0040 ownership warranty all survive without contradiction, because the new grant is a licence over deliverables rather than ownership of the Service or Auction Platform.

Drafting caution (not a failure): "deliverables provided under this Agreement" is lower-case and undefined in this MSA. Consider defining it or adding "(other than the Auction Platform, access to which is governed by Section 2)" so the perpetual, irrevocable, sublicensable grant cannot be read to override the expressly revocable, non-sublicensable platform licence in p0002/p0021.
